metrics.label: Bank Rate
metrics.detail: Held at 3.75% through 2026 — June MPC voted 7-2 to hold, July MPC held 6-3; next decision 17 September 2026
metrics.eclNote: Direct input to PD term structures and affordability overlays; a hold keeps debt-service stress on floating-rate BB borrowers elevated but stable

source.title: Bank of England — June 2026 Monetary Policy Summary (Bank Rate maintained at 3.75%)

metrics.label: CPI inflation
metrics.detail: ONS: CPI rose 3.4% in 12 months to December 2025, up from 3.2% in November; input value of 3.6% was October 2025 figure
metrics.eclNote: Feeds macroeconomic scenarios for forward-looking PD; cooling inflation supports rate-cut paths in the base case and eases cost pressure on SME margins

source.title: Consumer price inflation, UK: December 2025 | ONS

metrics.label: E&W company insolvencies (monthly)
metrics.detail: June 2026 E&W company insolvencies confirmed at 1,847 (not 1,845) per GOV.UK July 2026 release, which references June as the prior-month comparator; July 2026 itself was 1,931.
metrics.eclNote: Primary external benchmark for Stage 3 inflow and default-rate calibration in the BB book; falling counts support PD model back-testing and PMA release debates

source.title: Commentary - Company Insolvency Statistics July 2026 - GOV.UK

metrics.label: 2025 full-year insolvencies (E&W)
metrics.detail: Similar to 2024 (23,881); compulsory liquidations rose to highest annual number since 2012 while CVLs edged down
metrics.eclNote: Anchors through-the-cycle default assumptions; the compulsory-liquidation rise signals creditor (incl. HMRC) enforcement returning — a Stage 3 loss-given-default driver

source.title: Insolvency Service — Commentary, Company Insolvency Statistics December 2025

metrics.label: CVL share of insolvencies
metrics.detail: CVLs accounted for 78% of all company insolvencies in December 2025, up from 77% previously recorded.
metrics.eclNote: CVL-dominated mix means mostly small, low-asset failures — high LGD on unsecured BB exposure, low recoveries beyond the prescribed part

source.title: Company Insolvency Statistics December 2025 – The Gazette (Insolvency Service)

metrics.label: Company liquidation rate
metrics.detail: Full-year 2025 annual insolvency rate; one in 190 companies on the effective register entered insolvency in 2025, down from the rolling 52.9 seen at end-September 2025.
metrics.eclNote: The cleanest portfolio-level default-rate proxy for BB PD calibration; a falling rate supports benign base-case scenario weights

source.title: Commentary: Company Insolvency Statistics – December 2025 – GOV.UK

metrics.label: Gross SME bank lending 2025
metrics.detail: Gross SME bank lending rose 9% to £68bn in 2025, the second highest level in 13 years after the 2020 COVID peak, per the British Business Bank Small Business Finance Markets 2025/26 report.
metrics.eclNote: New origination grows EAD and dilutes seasoned-book default rates; vintage monitoring needed as 2025-26 cohorts season into 2027

source.title: Smaller business lending markets showing signs of improvement – British Business Bank

metrics.label: Challenger & specialist bank share
metrics.detail: Share of 2025 gross SME bank lending (39% in 2012); 68% including non-bank lenders
metrics.eclNote: Incumbent BB books are losing flow to challengers — survivor bias risk in incumbent PD data and adverse selection in retained risk profiles

source.title: British Business Bank — Small Business Finance Markets 2025/26 press release

metrics.label: SME bank lending stock
metrics.detail: Bank of England data via Ebury SME Borrowing Tracker: SME debt fell £4.4bn across 2024, from £175.4bn (Dec-2023) to £171.9bn (Dec-2024); British Business Bank Small Business Finance Markets 2024/25 also cites £171bn at Dec-24.
metrics.eclNote: The denominator for portfolio coverage and loss-rate metrics; run-off of legacy COVID debt shrinks EAD while flattering coverage ratios

source.title: SMEs Cut Debt by £4.4bn Across 2024 – FF News / Ebury SME Borrowing Tracker (Bank of England data)

metrics.label: BBLS total drawn
metrics.detail: GOV.UK COVID-19 loan guarantee schemes repayment data June 2025 release; prior March 2025 release showed £46.52bn. Stored asAt of 2026-03 appears erroneous.
metrics.eclNote: Defines the guaranteed legacy EAD pool in BB; 100% government guarantee means low LGD for the bank but heavy operational recovery/claim workload

source.title: COVID-19 loan guarantee schemes repayment data: June 2025 - GOV.UK

metrics.label: BBLS guarantee settled
metrics.detail: Share of BBLS facilities (by volume) with the government guarantee settled at 31 Mar 2026 — £11.82bn paid out, £1.58bn against suspected-fraud-flagged loans
metrics.eclNote: Settled claims crystallise Stage 3 outcomes without bank loss; watch clawback/assurance risk where guarantee conditions were breached — a residual LGD tail

source.title: GOV.UK — COVID-19 loan guarantee schemes repayment data: March 2026

metrics.label: Pay As You Grow take-up
metrics.detail: BBLS borrowers who have used at least one PAYG option (term extension to 10yrs, interest-only, or repayment holiday) at 31 Mar 2026; 46.95% of facilities on schedule, 19.38% fully repaid
metrics.eclNote: PAYG use is a forbearance-like SICR signal in all but name — extended 10-year tails push BBLS run-off into the 2030s and stretch lifetime ECL horizons

source.title: GOV.UK — COVID-19 loan guarantee schemes repayment data: March 2026

metrics.label: Barclays FY25 loan loss rate
metrics.detail: FY25 credit impairment charge £2,279m (FY24: £1,982m) — within 50-60bps through-the-cycle guidance; driven by GM portfolio acquisition, an IB single name and US macro uncertainty
metrics.eclNote: The group benchmark BB impairment rolls into; UK wholesale loss rates ran below the TTC range, so BB charges are being watched for normalisation not deterioration

metrics.label: Barclays H1 2026 loan loss rate
metrics.detail: H1 2026 group loan loss rate confirmed at 62bps; Q1 74bps (elevated by ~20bps GM portfolio single-name fraud charge), Q2 51bps — both within 50-60bps through-the-cycle guidance range.
metrics.eclNote: Above-range H1 print pressures the group ECL budget; BB staging and coverage assumptions face tighter challenge into Q3 (results 22 Oct 2026)

source.title: Barclays H1 2026 slides: RoTE hits 16.1% as income guidance rises — Investing.com

metrics.label: Growth Guarantee Scheme
metrics.value: 70% guarantee, to Mar 2030; facility terms up to 10 yrs (Term Loans & Asset Finance); turnover eligibility up to £54m; July 2026: additional £6.5bn lending capacity unlocked over next 4 years (est. 33,000 businesses supported)
metrics.detail: On 12 July 2026, Chancellor announced £6.5bn additional GGS capacity over 4 years; turnover uplift to £54m and 10-yr terms confirmed but pending operationalisation with accredited lenders.
metrics.eclNote: The 70% guarantee cuts LGD on covered new-lend; scheme extension keeps a guaranteed origination channel open through the Basel 3.1 transition

source.title: Growth Guarantee Scheme – British Business Bank

metrics.label: HMRC preference / prescribed part
metrics.detail: HMRC secondary preferential (VAT, PAYE, employee NIC, CIS) since 1 Dec 2020 with no cap; prescribed part for unsecured creditors capped at £800k for floating charges created on/after 6 Apr 2020
metrics.eclNote: HMRC ranks ahead of floating-charge realisations, directly depressing LGD recoveries on floating-charge-secured BB lending — a structural LGD assumption, not a cycle effect

source.title: Kirkland & Ellis — HMRC as Preferential Creditor takes effect 1 December 2020

metrics.label: Avg personal-guarantee-backed loan
metrics.detail: Purbeck Insurance Services Q4 2024 data: average PG-backed SME loan rose 9% to £174k from £159k in Q4 2023; £317,000 figure could not be verified in any official source.
metrics.eclNote: PGs are a second-way-out recovery assumption in BB LGD; rising guarantee sizes raise director exposure and realisation uncertainty in enforcement

source.title: Average personal guarantee backed loan rises 9% - Credit Connect

metrics.label: Starling SME banking share
metrics.detail: Starling holds roughly 9.7% of the UK SME banking market (600k+ business customers), targeting 12.5%
metrics.eclNote: Marks the competitive erosion of incumbent BCA primacy — losing the current-account data feed weakens incumbents' early-warning/SICR signal quality on shared customers

source.title: Business of Apps — Starling Bank Revenue and Usage Statistics (2026)

metrics.label: UK GDP growth (latest quarter)
metrics.detail: Strongest quarter since Q1 2025; services +0.8%. 2025 full-year growth 1.4%. Q2 2026 first estimate due 13 Aug 2026
metrics.eclNote: Core macroeconomic variable in ECL scenario sets; stronger growth shifts probability weight to the base/upside cases and supports PMA release pressure

source.title: ONS — GDP first quarterly estimate, UK: January to March 2026
